hints: Count the identical resistors in series with each ammeter: the $A_1$ loop has a vertical plus a horizontal resistor, while $A_3$ has one and $A_4$ has three.
Recall all three resistor branches connect between the same top wire and the same bottom wire as the cell, so they have the same p.d. $V = IR$.
Use $V = 0.6 \times 2R$ from the $A_1$ branch to find the currents $V/R$ and $V/3R$, then add the three branch currents to get $A_2$ by Kirchhoff's first law.
walkthrough: Let each resistor be $R$. The $A_1$ branch has $2R$ in series, the $A_3$ branch has $1R$, and the $A_4$ branch has $1R+2R = 3R$.
All three branches are in parallel across the cell, so they share the same p.d. $V$. From $A_1$, $V = I_1 \times 2R = 0.6 \times 2R = 1.2R$.
Ammeter $A_2$ is in the cell branch and carries the sum of the three parallel currents, so $I_2 = I_1+I_3+I_4 = 0.6+1.2+0.4 = 2.2 \text{ A}$.
Thus $A_2 = 2.2 \text{ A}$, $A_3 = 1.2 \text{ A}$, $A_4 = 0.4 \text{ A}$. This is option D.

A.explanation: These values are too small because they do not give the same p.d. across the $2R$, $R$ and $3R$ branches.

B.explanation: The $A_3$ current is not equal to $A_1$ because the $A_3$ branch has only one resistor while the $A_1$ branch has two in series.

C.explanation: These ratios $0.6:0.9:0.3$ do not match the inverse resistance ratio $1/2:1:1/3$ for parallel branches with the same p.d.
